tests.name: Lake at rest over bumpy terrain + island + building (well-balanced)
tests.reference: exact: u = 0, η = const (Audusse et al. 2004 well-balanced property)
tests.result: max |u| 9.9e-08 m/s, max |Δη| 6.0e-08 m after 1 h; 1b perturbed pool surface range 4.1e-06 m (alpha 0.6); HLL option: lake max |u| 8.2e-14 m/s, pool range 8.4e-07 m
tests.tolerance: |u| < 1e-3 m/s, |Δη| < 1 mm; 1b: 1 mm bump stays < 2 mm
tests.notes: Wet/dry fronts around the island and a solid building included. 1b exposes a CFL instability at alpha = 0.7 (validation/BUGS.md B1); alpha <= 0.6 is stable.

tests.name: Mass conservation, real grid, full dec31_2022 storm
tests.reference: rain in = surface + sewer storage + infiltration + treatment + CSO + edge + bay exchange
tests.result: closure 3.7e-09 % of 1.25 Mm³ rain; rain vs independent integral -0.000 %; surface vs frames -0.00 %
tests.notes: Closure uses the solver's own flux ledger; rain input and final surface storage are re-derived independently (hyetograph integral x land area; sum of the saved final depth frame). Replay parameters: scheme inertial, i_design 10.3 mm/h, alpha 0.6

tests.name: 1D dam break vs Stoker (wet bed) / Ritter (dry bed), both water schemes
tests.reference: Stoker 1957 / Ritter 1892 analytic; local-inertial expected weaker at high Froude (Bates 2010; de Almeida & Bates 2013 WRR 49)
tests.result: inertial: h_r/h_l 0.5 err 3.5 %/front -14 %, h_r/h_l 0.1 err 10.8 %/front -31 %, h_r/h_l 0.0 err 12.0 %/front -58 %; hll: h_r/h_l 0.5 err 1.0 %/front -0 %, h_r/h_l 0.1 err 1.2 %/front -2 %, h_r/h_l 0.0 err 1.2 %/front -15 %
tests.tolerance: mean |err| < 5 % of h_l and bore position within 10 %; verdict on the production scheme ('inertial'), subcritical case h_r/h_l = 0.5
tests.notes: Local-inertial drops the advection term, so it converges to a slightly different PDE: its error does not shrink with dx (dx 4 m 3.50 %, dx 2 m 3.46 %, dx 1 m 3.49 %) and grows with Froude; the dry-bed front is far too slow. The full-SWE HLL option (Audusse 2004 hydrostatic reconstruction) fixes this: dx 4 m 1.02 %, dx 2 m 0.62 %, dx 1 m 0.37 % on the same case, and it captures the dry-bed front. Urban ponding (the damage driver) is low-Froude.

tests.name: Steady uniform flow on a sloped channel vs Manning normal depth, both schemes
tests.tolerance: subcritical (Fr < 0.8): |err| < 1 % and steady; verdict on production scheme 'inertial'
tests.notes: Local-inertial: exact (0.0x %) for subcritical flow; at Fr ≥ ~0.9 (steep SF streets, thin sheet flow) spurious roll-wave oscillations and a mean depth 15-35 % low (BUGS.md B2). HLL: always steady, but first-order hydrostatic reconstruction over-predicts thin flow on steep slopes (a known issue when h << slope x dx, Delestre et al. 2012; BUGS.md B4) and is 1.7 % low on the rough mild case. Ponding that drives damage is subcritical.

tests.name: EA 2D benchmark Test 1/Test 2-type (disconnected water body; filling depressions)
tests.reference: Néelz & Pender 2013 (EA SC120002) test behaviours; own DEMs, exact level-pool answers
tests.result: (a) pond peak 10.366 m vs 10.35, final 10.010 m vs 10.00; (b) end levels A +0.5 cm, B +0.8 cm, C +0.8 cm, D -1.0 cm; volume err -4.6e-08 %

tests.name: Replay vs SFPUC 100-year storm flood zone

tests.result: CSI 0.27 (random same-area 0.05, lowest-ground 0.14); POD 0.42, FAR 0.56; AUC 0.72
tests.tolerance: CSI > 2x random same-area map and AUC > 0.7
tests.notes: The SFPUC zone is SFPUC's own model of a 100-year design storm, not an observation. The replay forcing (SFOC1 gauge: 88 mm in 6 h, 67 mm in 3 h) is ~200-yr (6 h) / ~300-yr (3 h) by NOAA Atlas 14 at SF, so the 100-yr zone should mostly flood (POD is the key number) and some extra flooding outside it is expected. tests.result: 83% within 30 m of sim flooding vs 60% random (p = 0.0001); depth AUC 0.63 (p = 5.2e-09)

tests.name: Poiseuille channel flow (wind LBM kernel)
tests.reference: Analytic Poiseuille parabola u = F/(2 nu) (2 H z - z^2), nu = (tau - 1/2)/3
tests.notes: Laminar check of the production lbm_step (regularized BGK, half-way bounce-back floor, specular lid) with Smagorinsky off (cs2=0) and a body force added outside the kernel; 16 cells across the half channel. Verifies collision viscosity and wall placement, not the turbulence model.

tests.name: Log-law inflow profile upstream of an obstacle
tests.reference: U(z)/U10 = ln((z+z0)/z0)/ln((10+z0)/z0), z0 = 0.7 m; horizontal homogeneity requirement of Blocken, Stathopoulos & Carmeliet 2007 (Atmos. Environ. 41:238)
tests.result: max deviation 10-200 m: 5.7 % at 3H upstream (4.9 % at inlet)
tests.notes: Profiles are spanwise means from the cube run (5H = 320 m fetch from the domain inflow through the 96 m buffer). The first fluid cell (4 m) is below the 10 m band. The 3H station is also affected by the cube's upstream blockage near the ground.

tests.name: Flow around a surface-mounted cube (full wind solver)
tests.reference: Reattachment X_R = 1.61 H (Martinuzzi & Tropea 1993, J. Fluids Eng. 115:85, thin-BL channel); the recirculation shortens in a thick turbulent BL (Castro & Robins 1977, JFM 79:307). Front-face Cp_max ~0.7-0.9 on U_H (Castro & Robins 1977; Richards et al. 2001 Silsoe cube)
tests.result: X_R 2.96 H; front Cp_max 0.93; Cd 0.69; grid study X_R 2.50 (8/H), 2.10 (16/H)
tests.tolerance: X_R in 1.0-2.5 H; front Cp_max in 0.5-1.0

grid_convergence.status: not run: 2.2 M cells x 7.5k steps needs ~1 h on the shared box, did not fit before code freeze

tests.notes: Grid convergence (same 64 m cube, dx = 64/n m, smaller 8.5H x 6H x 2.5H domain, ~7 % blockage): 8 cells/H: X_R 2.50 H, Cd 0.83; 16 cells/H: X_R 2.10 H, Cd 0.81; 24 cells/H: not run: 2.2 M cells x 7.5k steps needs ~1 h on the shared box, did not fit before code freeze. X_R falls with every refinement (2.50 -> 2.10 H) towards the 1.61 H measurement, consistent with the base-case excess being a resolution error (only 2 levels, so no Richardson extrapolation claimed). The base run's longer X_R in the larger domain also shows some domain sensitivity. Same run_lbm as the city (8 m voxels, Smagorinsky LES, log-law inflow z0 0.7 m, wall-modelled floor, time-averaged field). 64 m cube = 8 cells per H, coarse by LES standards (Martinuzzi & Tropea is Re 4e4 in a channel with a thin BL; our inflow is a deep urban log-law BL), so agreement is expected only within the stated band. Cd from front minus back mean Cp (pressure drag, U_H reference). If X_R is long, the likely causes are the coarse 8 cells/H resolution with Smagorinsky dissipation (a too-laminar shear layer reattaches late, as in standard k-epsilon RANS, which gives ~2.5-3 H; cf. Rodi 1997, J. Wind Eng. 69-71:55) and the free-slip + wall-model floor. Impact on the product: street-level speeds in building wakes (sheltered zones) are less reliable than speeds in open canyons and at facades.

tests.name: Tree critical breaking wind speed (calibration consistency)
tests.reference: Virot, Ponomarenko, Dehandschoewercker, Quere & Clanet 2016, Phys. Rev. E 93:023001: trunks break at ~42 m/s nearly independent of species and size
tests.result: median 42.0 m/s (p10 19.2, p90 84.3); log-log slope vs height 0.17
tests.tolerance: median within 42 +/- 8 m/s (calibrated) and weak size dependence |d ln Uc / d ln H| < 0.5 (independent)
tests.notes: HONEST LIMIT: the median is not a prediction: tree_load_factor (2.9) and tree_cd0 in data/reference/wind_tree_params.json were calibrated to put it at 42 m/s. The independent part is the size dependence (Virot: near-universal Uc) and that each bundled factor sits in its published range; our p10-p90 spread (species wood strength, crown shape) is much wider than Virot's. Dry-soil uprooting thresholds are far lower (see validation/BUGS.md W1). Computed for sound wood (decay factor removed) on the real tile inventory, exactly as sim.trees.virot_check. Virot's 42 m/s is a 10-min-ish mean speed at the crown from storm records; our Uc is the crown speed from the drag/Vogel model. Decayed trees and uprooting on saturated soil fail at lower speeds in the sim by design.
